papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.abstract: We introduce LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters. In particular, LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 (175B) on most benchmarks, and LLaMA-65B is competitive with the best models, Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B. We release all our models to the research community.

report_markdown:
## Overview
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has become essential for adapting large language models (LLMs) to downstream tasks while drastically reducing computational and storage overhead [13,36,41]. Despite rapid progress in PEFT methodologies, significant gaps persist in specialized domains, continual learning, and generalization, limiting the full potential of these techniques.

## Landscape
The PEFT landscape encompasses a variety of methods that update only a small subset of parameters, such as adapters, LoRA, prefix tuning, prompt tuning, and BitFit [13,17,22,30,34,40,42]. Comprehensive surveys provide taxonomies, comparative analyses, and practical guidelines for selecting and applying these methods [36,41,45]. Tools like LlamaFactory and LLM-Adapters streamline the implementation of PEFT across many models [27,30]. Domain-specific adaptation is an active area, with efforts in medicine and mental health beginning to explore PEFT, though challenges like task variety and data imbalance remain [7,32,43]. Continual learning with PEFT is emerging, but current work is largely confined to prompt-based approaches [44,48]. Prompt tuning methods, while effective, often suffer from reduced zero-shot generalization when trained on domain-specific data [37,40]. Federated learning frameworks have also started to incorporate PEFT to enable privacy-preserving fine-tuning [38].

## Research gaps
- **Mental health prediction**: There is a significant gap in applying and evaluating PEFT methods for mental health tasks. Existing systematic reviews of NLP in mental health [20,24] and recent LLM evaluations [32] highlight the lack of PEFT-focused studies in this domain.
- **Continual learning beyond prompts**: In continual learning, PEFT methods other than prompt tuning (e.g., Adapter, LoRA, Prefix) remain largely unexplored, restricting applicability to Transformer architectures only [44,48].
- **Zero-shot generalization in prompt tuning**: Prompt tuning methods exhibit degraded generalization to unseen domains when trained on domain-specific data, underscoring the need for techniques that preserve zero-shot capabilities [37].
- **Multi-task medical applications**: Existing fine-tuning methods, including PEFT, struggle with task variety and data imbalance in multi-task medical settings, leading to sub-optimal performance [43].
